body: Key-value (KV) cache eviction is essential for scaling long-context inference in Large Language Models. However, existing policies predominantly rely on empirical heuristics, lacking a rigorous characterization of token utility under the inherently nonlinear softmax attention mechanism. In this work, we rethink KV cache eviction through the lens of local information geometry, modeling the attention process as a nonlinear Gaussian communication channel. By performing a first-order Taylor expansion of the attention mapping, we derive the Jacobian Information Capacity, a novel objective that explicitly captures query relevance, softmax sensitivity, and structural diversity. Guided by this theory, we introduce Jacap, a capacity-aware eviction method that utilizes softmax-aware importance weighting and statistical leverage scores for subset selection. Extensive experiments across diverse architectures and benchmarks demonstrate that Jacap delivers superior performance in most scenarios, particularly in high-compression regimes.
summaryZh: 该研究针对大型语言模型（LLM）长上下文推理中的关键值（KV）缓存淘汰问题，提出了一种名为Jacap的容量感知淘汰方法。现有策略多依赖经验启发式，缺乏对非线性softmax注意力机制下token效用的严谨刻画。Jacap将注意力过程建模为非线性高斯通信信道，通过泰勒展开推导出雅可比信息容量（Jacobian Information Capacity）这一新目标，显式捕捉查询相关性、softmax敏感性和结构多样性。实验表明，Jacap在多种架构和基准测试中表现优越，尤其在高压缩率场景下。
